purpose: test whether dense recovery updates let the confirmed low-max-abs allocator improve the total-cost frontier rather than only beat uniform random sparsity
reused_frozen_references: uniform low_max_abs, uniform random, dense, and dense-fewer from results-program/dev-long with identical body and online seeds
sparse_evaluation: uniform low_max_abs or random at the original average budget, never the anchor schedule
primary_endpoints: anchored low_max_abs minus anchored random sparse loss at every evaluation
anchored low_max_abs minus uniform low_max_abs sparse loss at every evaluation
anchored low_max_abs minus dense-fewer at matched total cost including auxiliary operations
dense evaluation, realized average activity, and per-schedule costs

selection_rule.allocation_and_schedule_benefit: a schedule must beat its random-anchor control and uniform low_max_abs at step 200 in all four regimes
selection_rule.schedule_selection: if both schedules qualify, select the one with the smallest mean final loss difference from uniform low_max_abs
selection_rule.development_level_3_signal: the selected schedule must also beat dense-fewer at matched total cost in all four regimes
selection_rule.kill: if neither schedule satisfies allocation_and_schedule_benefit, stop anchor tuning; if none beats dense-fewer, do not claim a practical frontier opening
selection_rule.fresh_confirmation: only a selected schedule with a development Level 3 signal earns an unchanged fresh-to-schedule replication on bodies 9 and 10

prohibited: changing anchor frequency or non-anchor budgets after seeing results
comparing anchored low_max_abs only with uniform random
using anchored inference to inflate the sparse-training comparison
calling an improvement over uniform low_max_abs a Level 3 result without a dense-fewer win
